summary:
**Earth Detective** is an interactive web platform developed by the ASTRALISS team to study long‑term changes in Earth’s climate indicators based on open scientific data from NASA.

The problem is that climate data are available, but searching for, processing, and statistically interpreting them requires special knowledge.

We have developed an app with an interactive 2D/3D map where the user can select any point on Earth and examine changes in air temperature and specific humidity for the period from 1991 to 2025. The data is received via NASA POWER, and global temperature maps are displayed using NASA GIBS.

Earth Detective automatically calculates annual indicators, identifies linear trends, assesses their statistical significance, and visualizes the results. The user can also compare two geographical locations.

Our solution makes NASA’s scientific data more accessible to schoolchildren, students, teachers, and researchers, helping them not just to observe the changes.
details:
Earth Detective — project details

Earth Detective is an interactive science and education web platform developed by the ASTRALISS team to study long‑term changes in Earth’s atmospheric indicators using open NASA data.

How does the project work?

The user selects a geographical point on an interactive 2D/3D map or via search. The app sends the coordinates to the backend, which accesses the NASA POWER API and retrieves historical monthly data on air temperature (T2M) and specific humidity (QV2M) for 1991–2025.

The obtained data are processed using mathematical algorithms. The system calculates average annual values, determines the linear trend using the OLS method, and assesses its statistical significance using HAC/Newey–West, p-value, and a 95% confidence interval.

The results are displayed in the form of interactive graphs and clear scientific conclusions. The user can also compare the indicators of two geographical locations. For global visualization of the temperature.
